title: Celebrations & Party
strapline: Blow out the candles — three, two, one!
intent: Parties and celebrations are joyful shared events every child recognises, so the play is instantly warm and inclusive.
Celebrations from many homes and cultures can be woven in, helping children see and value what is special to their friends and families.
Setting up, inviting, sharing food and giving gifts is full of fair-share number, counting and one-to-one matching.
Invitations, cards, lists and labels give writing a real and happy job.
Planning and hosting a party is cooperation in action — everyone with a part to play.
implementation: Provide the makings of a party — a table, plates and cups, pretend food, candles, hats, wrapping and cards.
Take a guest role so children host, invite, serve and share.
Model the planning talk: 'How many friends are coming? So how many plates do we need?'
Bring in family celebrations children know — birthdays, Eid, Diwali, Christmas, Lunar New Year — led by what the children and families share.
Leave invitations, a guest list and card-making materials so writing has a purpose.
Draw out one-to-one matching and fair shares: a cup for each guest, the cake split evenly.
key_questions: Who will you invite, and how many are coming?
How many cups and plates do we need so everyone has one?
How can we share the cake so it's fair for everyone?
What celebrations happen at your house — what do you do?
What could you write on the invitation so your friends know when to come?

impact.text: Children match one-to-one — a plate, cup and hat for each guest — and count out what's needed.
Children share food fairly and talk about everyone getting the same.
Children host and take part together, cooperating to set up and run the party.
Children talk about celebrations from their own families and show interest in their friends' special days.
Children make invitations, cards and lists, mark-making that carries a real message.
Children join in songs, dancing and celebrating together with obvious delight.

enhancements: A party table with cloth, plates, cups, cutlery and pretend food.
Card- and invitation-making materials, a guest list and a post box.
Wrapping paper, boxes and ribbon for making and giving gifts.
Music, instruments and space for party dancing.
Objects, foods and stories from families' real celebrations (shared with parents).
A candle-and-cake counting game: light and blow out the right number.

playing_exploring: Children replay happy, familiar events and bring their own family experiences into the play.
They throw themselves into the fun of hosting and celebrating.
active_learning: Children plan and set up the whole party, seeing the preparations through to the celebration.
creating_thinking: Children solve how many guests, plates and shares are needed, and invent their own celebrations.
